pages.title: The Dump Chest
pages.text: Coming home from a mining trip, the first thing you want is to empty your inventory. Hoppers work, but they only pull from the top and they are slow.$(br2)An $(item)Extractor Module$() constantly pulls items out of whatever it is attached to and injects them into the network to be sunk. Put one in a Chassis on a chest and dump everything there.

pages.title: Making It Fast
pages.text: Out of the box the module is $(italic)slower$() than a hopper: one item every five seconds.$(br2)$(item)Item Extraction Upgrades$() raise how many items it moves each time; $(item)Action Speed Upgrades$() raise how often it runs.$(br2)marth uses five or six Action Speed and a few more Item Extraction for a dump chest. Both cap at 16. Remember that extraction costs power.

pages.title: Upgrading a Module
pages.text: The $(item)Pipe Controller$() will not help here: these upgrades go on the $(italic)module$(), not the Chassis.$(br2)Craft a $(item)Module Upgrade$(). Installed in a Chassis, it adds a row of slots to the right of every module — that is where module upgrades go. Open it with the $(item)Pipe Manager$().

pages.title: Where Else They Help
pages.text: Item Extraction Upgrades also work on $(item)Provider$() and $(item)Crafting Pipes$(), and on Provider and Crafting Modules.$(br2)That matters when something requests an enormous quantity: the extraction speed of the pipe itself becomes the bottleneck.

pages.title: Item Sink Priority
pages.text: When more than one pipe can sink an item, the network decides by priority:$(br)$(li)$(item)Passive Supplier Modules$()$(li)Item Sinks — Basic Pipes and all ItemSink Modules$(li)$(item)Terminus Modules$()$(li)Default routes

pages.title: Passive Suppliers
pages.text: $(item)Passive Supplier Modules$() are largely a relic from before Active Suppliers existed.$(br2)They try to keep a number of an item in stock, but unlike $(item)Supplier Pipes$() and $(item)Active Supplier Modules$() they never $(italic)request$() anything. They simply grab what they need first when it enters the network.

pages.title: Terminus Modules
pages.text: With their below-normal priority, $(item)Terminus Modules$() are how you get rid of excess once storage fills up.$(br2)Most networks have one dumping surplus cobblestone and dirt into a trash can, a matter condenser, or a pool of lava — so it never crowds out the default route's storage.

pages.title: Why the Default Route Fills Up
pages.text: Supplier and Crafting Pipes are absent from that list. Suppliers use active routing, which can only request from providers; Basic pipes and other sinks use passive routing, which can only react to items already in the network.$(br2)So the default route may never empty itself, even with a provider on it — there is no priority system for providers. Fill it and the network starts spilling items on the floor.

pages.title: QuickSort Modules
pages.text: A $(item)QuickSort Module$() looks at what it holds and searches for somewhere on the network — other than a default route — that can sink it. If it finds one, it puts the item back into the network to be re-sunk.$(br2)Upgrade the default route's Chassis to Mk3 and add one.

pages.title: Using It
pages.text: Check the chest now and then for anything piling up. When something is, take one out and place it in a chest with a $(item)Polymorphic sink$() — QuickSort will move the rest across.$(br2)Or add it to a $(item)Terminus Module$() and have QuickSort send it off for disposal.

pages.title: QuickSort as a Dump Chest
pages.text: QuickSort Modules also make good alternatives to Extractor Modules for the post-outing dump chest. They do not extract items that have nowhere but the default route to go, which makes it immediately obvious when something needs storage.$(br2)In most of marth's factories the default route and the dump chest are the same chest.

pages.title: A Warning
pages.text: $(bold)Do not place a QuickSort Module in the same place as an item sink$() unless that sink is a default route.$(br2)And if you ignore that, do not do it twice in one network — the QuickSort Modules will trade items back and forth forever.
